∡ denotes directed angles modulo 180°. Let ω₂ be the circle (CNR), with center O₂; P lies on ω₂. Let F be the foot of the perpendicular from B to AR. Angles written ∠ are undirected and read as drawn.

Claim 1. F, N, B, A are concyclic.

Proof. ∡BFA = 90° = ∡BNA (BF ⟂ AR; BC is a diameter), so F, N, B, A are concyclic.

Claim 2. FN = BF.

Proof. ∡FAN = ∡BAF (AR bisects ∠BAC). By equal arcs and chords (Claim 1), FN = BF.

Claim 3. R, N, F, O are concyclic.

Proof.

∡RFN = ∡BFN + 90°    [BF ⟂ AR]
     = 2∡FBN + 90°    [FB = FN (Claim 2)]
     = 2∡FAN + 90°    [inscribed angles in (ABNF) (Claim 1)]
     = ∡BAC + 90°    [AR bisects ∠BAC]
     = ∡MCN    [BC is a diameter]

As drawn, ∠MCN = ½·∠MON = ∠RON (central angle ∠MON = 2∠MCN; OR bisects ∠MON), so R, N, F, O are concyclic.

Claim 4. A, F, R, P are collinear.

Proof. AB·AM = AC·AN (power of A with respect to (BMCN)). By the radical axis theorem (P, R, M, B concyclic; P, R, N, C on ω₂; A, B, M collinear; A, N, C collinear), A, F, R, P are collinear.

∡RAB = ∡FNB = ∡NFO + 90° (Claim 1; OF is the perpendicular bisector of BN (Claim 2)).

∡PCB = ∡ARP + ∡PCB    [Claim 4]
     = ∡NCB + ∡ARN    [P, R, N, C on ω₂]
     = ∡MBO + ∡(CN, OR) + 90°    [Claim 3, ∡RAB = ∡NFO + 90°, shown above]
     = ∡CNB + 90°    [OR bisects ∠MON, OB = OM = ON]
     = ∡CMB + 90°    [inscribed angles in (BCMN)]
     = 0°    [BC is a diameter]

so P, B, C are collinear. ∎
